summary: Lisa N. Owen works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She earned her Ph.D. from the University of Texas at Austin under doctoral supervisor Janice Leoshko, and also studied under Walter M. Spink in 1995.

Lita Peipina specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Jens-Uwe Hartmann and completed an MA at the University of Oslo (attested 2008), where she was supervised by Jens Braarvig in 2003.

Litian Fang (1933–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. After studying at Peking University under Feng Youlan, Yongtong Tang, and Zhang Dainian (~1957–1961), he served as professor, doctoral supervisor, and founding director at Renmin University of China (~1961–2014).

Lloyd W. Pflueger is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University (attested 2015).

Lobsang Dargyay (1935–1994) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Rahor Monastery, Drepung Monastery (~1952–1959), and completed his Dr.phil. at the University of Munich (~1969–1974).

Lobsang Gyatso (1928–1997) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso and served as head of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics from ~1973 to 1997.

Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa (1926–2008) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Dudjom Rinpoche, Trijang Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Drubwang Shakya Shri.

Lobsang Sangay (born 1968) is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He studied at the University of Delhi (~1988–1995) and Harvard Law School (~1995–2004), later serving as a researcher at Harvard University (~2004–2011).

Lobsang Shastri works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as Head Librarian of the Tibetan Section at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 2003–2006) and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (attested 2018).

Lobsang Tendzin (born 1939) is a Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Drepung and Gyuto monasteries, he taught at Central Schools for Tibetans (1961–1970) and served as director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1977–2000).

Lobsang Tenpa specializes in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history and archaeology. He earned a Master of Philosophy degree at Jawaharlal Nehru University under the supervision of Sharad K. Soni.

Lobsang Tenzin (born 1937) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology educated at Drepung Monastery. He led Central School for Tibetans (1965–1970) and served as principal and director of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1971; 1988–2001).

Lobsang Yongdan works in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Kumbum Monastery and earned a PhD from the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger, later holding postdoctoral posts at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science and University of Bonn.

Loden Sherab Dagyab (born 1940) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Monastery and under the 14th Dalai Lama, Ling Rinpoche, and Trijang Rinpoche, worked at the University of Bonn (1966), and founded Tibet House Germany (2005).

Loden Sherap Dagyab Rinpoche (born 1940) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Drepung Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche and Ling Rinpoche, he directed Tibet House New Delhi (1964–1966), worked at the University of Bonn (1966), and founded Tibet House Germany (2005).
Lodrö Chökyi Sengé was a scholar who studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche, and also taught Kalu Rinpoche.

Lodrö Sangpo (born 1953) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under Ernst Steinkellner, founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996, and served as a senior teacher at the Vidyadhara Institute (attested 2008).

Lokesh Chandra (born 1927) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Educated at the University of the Punjab and Utrecht University, he led the International Academy of Indian Culture (~1950–1963) and chaired the Indian Council of Historical Research (~2014–2017).
Longlian (1909–2006) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under Fazun beginning in 1939 and also studied under Nenghai Shi.

Lopon Tenzin Namdak (born 1926) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tingchen, Yungdrung Ling, and Menri monasteries. He served as lopön at Menri Monastery (1953–1959, 1978) and founded Triten Norbutse Monastery in 1986.
